subject.title: PR4/5 durable core: wake controls, inspection, CLI, and Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in durable runtime stack in core and on the 2026.7.1 release line, including its shared SQLite schema and public CLI, Gateway, and plugin SDK contracts?
rationale: The patch is not merely a bounded bug fix: it establishes persistent state ownership and several long-lived public surfaces whose scope, release timing, and compatibility policy require maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor inspection-first core
options.body: Accept the durable-core direction while keeping PR4 read-only publicly, contingent on exact-head enabled-runtime and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to architecture only
options.body: Keep the RFC and test-plan work but defer runtime, schema, CLI, Gateway, and SDK adoption to a later sponsored release program.

options.title: Decline the core direction
options.body: Close the stack and retain existing task, session, audit, and delivery owners without adding a general durable runtime substrate.

recommendation.title: Sponsor inspection-first core
recommendation.body: Accept the durable-core direction while keeping PR4 read-only publicly, contingent on exact-head enabled-runtime and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core architecture, release ownership, persistence, Gateway API, CLI, and plugin SDK policy rather than one isolated subsystem.
